-47: Caesar's siege of Alexandria. Julius Caesar was besieged in the city in 47 BCE, and the royal Library was damaged in the fighting. Octavian (Augustus) later placed the city under a Roman prefect.
2002: Bibliotheca Alexandrina inaugurated. A new library and cultural centre, built on the seafront near the harbour to a design by Snohetta, opened in October 2002.

1886: Goldfield proclaimed and town laid out. After gold was found on the farm Langlaagte, President Kruger declared the area open for public diggings on 20 September 1886. A town was surveyed beside Ferreira's Camp and named Johannesburg.

2010: World Cup final and Gautrain. The rebuilt Soccer City (FNB Stadium) hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup final. The Gautrain rapid rail link to Sandton, the airport and Pretoria, begun in 2006, was completed in June 2012.
